title: An Octopus Has 3 Hearts and Blue Blood!
question: Did you know octopuses have three hearts and blue blood?
answer: An octopus has three hearts, and its blood is blue because it uses copper to carry oxygen.
description: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood! Find out what each heart does and why the blood is blue, in under a minute.

visual.what: A friendly octopus floats on a coral reef. Three small glowing hearts pop up on its body, and a drop of blue blood shines beside it.

parts.text: Did you know an octopus has three hearts and blue blood?
Three hearts? I only have one!

visual.what: Cutaway cartoon of an octopus. Two hearts sit beside the gills, with arrows from each heart into the gills. Water bubbles flow past the gills.

parts.text: Two hearts send blood to the gills. Gills are how an octopus takes oxygen from the water.

visual.what: Same octopus. The third, bigger heart in the middle pumps blood with arrows out to the head and all eight arms.

parts.text: The third heart pumps blood to the rest of the body.
So every heart has its own job!

visual.what: Split picture. Left, a child's arm with red blood and a little iron nail icon. Right, an octopus arm with blue blood and a copper coin icon.

parts.text: Your blood is red because it carries oxygen with iron.

visual.what: Zoom into a blue drop of octopus blood. Tiny orange copper dots hold small bubbles of oxygen. Hùng holds a copper coin and drops it with a clink.

parts.text: Octopus blood uses copper instead. Copper makes the blood blue when it carries oxygen.
Oops, I dropped my copper coin!
But it is orange, not blue!

visual.what: Huy, Hùng, Bối and Beo wave beside the octopus. A big heart count of three and a blue drop float above. A Follow Ask Huy button pulses.

parts.text: Three hearts and blue blood. Wow! Follow Ask Huy for more amazing facts!

facts.claim: Octopuses have three hearts. Two pump blood to the gills, and the third pumps it to the rest of the body.
Octopus blood carries oxygen with hemocyanin, a protein that contains copper. It turns blue when it holds oxygen.
Human blood is red because of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen and contains iron.
Hemocyanin was first found in Octopus vulgaris in 1878.
